prompt: A candle burns at a constant rate. After $2$ hours it is $18$ cm tall, and after $5$ hours it is $10.5$ cm tall. What was the height of the candle, in centimeters, before it was lit?
hint: Constant rate means a linear model. Find the rate first.

hints.text: Constant rate means a linear model. Find the rate first.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try an easier pair: after $1$ hour a candle is $9$ cm and after $2$ hours it is $7$ cm, so it burns $2$ cm per hour. Running back one hour from the 9 cm mark gives $11$ cm at the start.
It lost $18 - 10.5 = 7.5$ cm over $3$ hours, so it burns $2.5$ cm per hour.
Run back $2$ hours from the 18 cm mark: $18 + 2(2.5) = 23$ cm.

learningObjective: Extrapolate a linear model backwards to its initial value.
explanation: The rate of change is $\dfrac{10.5 - 18}{5 - 2} = \dfrac{-7.5}{3} = -2.5$ cm per hour.
"Before it was lit" means $t = 0$, which is $2$ hours before the 18 cm reading.

alternativeExplanations.title: Write the equation
steps: The initial height is the $y$-intercept, which the equation now displays directly: $23$ cm.
The trap is answering $-2.5$ or $18$ — both appear in the setup, neither is the initial height.
